4"1(a) Restoration of Degraded Forest Land.

Forest loss and degradation exacerbate local and global problems related to food and livelihoods, clean water, fresh air and the climate. Degraded landscapes are also more vulnerable to natural disasters and extreme weather conditions, such as heavy rainfall, floods and landslides. Forest Land Restoration has great potential to address these issues by enhancing landscapes in ways that ensure lasting benefits. Benefits include better local climate regulations, improved flood and erosion control, an increased variety and availability of food and non-food products and economic opportunities for local people. Reducing emissions from deforestation and degradation in the forest areas is yet another challenge in combating the adverse impact of the Climate Change on biodiversity conservation and protection. Forest land restoration can support climate change mitigation and adaptation, while enhancing ecological and livelihood values for the landscape and its people.

The forest cover of the State as per the ISFR 2019 has sequestrated 216 Million tonnes (Mt) of carbon which is 3.03% of the total carbon stock of 7,124 Mt stored in

lndia's forest cover. Therefore, through the Green Tamil Nadu Mission, the State of Tamil Nadu has proposed to enhance the carbon sequestration potential on an average of 8 Mt every year from the year 2024-2025 to 2030-2031 by increasing the forest & tree cover. lt is expected that the carbon stock can be built up to about 265 - 270 Mt, in the year 2031 from a base year of 2019. this department. Besides, the Tribal Research

Centre at the Nilgiris district is conducting

research on the language and culture of

Scheduled Tribes.

For the integrated socio-economic and

educational development of Adi Dravidar,

Schemes such as, running of Adi Dravidar Welfare

schools, hostels, issuing house site pattas and

improving basic amenities in Adi Dravidar

habitations are being implemented through the

Commissionerate of Adi Dravidar Welfare.

For the advancement of the Scheduled

Tribes, Schemes like running Government Tribal

Residential Schools and hostels, establishing basic

infrastructure facilities in their habitations,

implementation of the Forest Rights Act and

implementing schemes for their economic

4

developments are implemented by the

Directorate of Tribal Welfare.

The Tamil Nadu Adi Dravidar Housing and

Development Corporation Limited (TAHDCO) is

implementing subsidized loan schemes for the

economic development and imparting various skill

development trainings to create self-employment

/ employment opportunities for youth people

belonging to Adi Dravidar and Scheduled Tribe

communities.

Implementation of the Scheduled Castes

and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)

Act, enacted for the protection of the rights and

prevention of atrocities against these

marginalized communities of the society is

monitored by the Social Justice and Human Rights

Wing of Police.

Apart from the above, a new autonomous

body, “Tamil Nadu State Commission for Adi

Dravidar and Scheduled Tribes” has been

5

created to protect the legal rights of Adi Dravidar

and Scheduled Tribes at the State Level and to

address their important issues.

A State Level Vigilance and Monitoring

Committee has been constituted under the

Chairmanship of the Hon’ble Chief Minister to

review the implementation of Protection of Civil

Rights Act 1955 and Scheduled Castes and

Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

Apart from these Committees, Welfare

Boards such as, Tamil Nadu Puthirai Vannar

Welfare Board to ensure that the welfare

schemes of the Government and other benefits to

reach the Puthirai Vannar community people,

Tamil Nadu Tribal Welfare Board to monitor

the benefits for the welfare of the Scheduled

Tribes, Tamil Nadu Sanitary Workers Board to

monitor the implementation of schemes meant for

the welfare of sanitary workers are functioning

under the control of this department.
